key_insight: The paper reframes safety in meta-RL as reachability in an information space that combines the agent’s physical state and belief about the task, enabling a learnable safety value function.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to add safety constraints during rapid task adaptation, which is important for deploying meta-RL in robotics and other safety-critical systems.
method: Define an information-space safety value that estimates the probability of avoiding unsafe regions indefinitely.
Show the value satisfies a self-consistency condition and Bellman equation, making it suitable for learning.
Use the learned safety value for safety filtering and constrained policy optimization during adaptation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on meta-RL benchmarks, indicating the method was evaluated empirically and showed effectiveness.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurately modeling and learning belief-state safety, so performance may be sensitive to uncertainty estimation and task distribution shift.
paper_title: Safe Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Information Space Reachability
